strengths: Addresses an important practical problem with a coherent combination of distilled security guidelines, patch-focused program slicing, and security-aware retrieval.
Table 1 reports higher SecurePass@1 than every evaluated baseline across all six models, with improvements of 2.5–13.6 percentage points over unaugmented generation.
Jointly measuring functional correctness and security avoids rewarding nonfunctional code merely because it passes static security checks.
The experiments include multiple model families, three additional functionality benchmarks, extensive component ablations, alternative summarization models, and a latency breakdown.
weaknesses: Security evidence comes exclusively from 94 CodeGuard+ scenarios evaluated with CodeQL; the other three benchmarks measure only functionality. No independent security validation or task-level confidence intervals establish the robustness of the gains. Section 3.3.2 also explicitly selects k using CodeGuard+ results without reporting a separate validation split.

The contribution primarily combines established summarization, slicing, hierarchical retrieval, and rank-fusion techniques. Missing controls—including security-aware prompting or self-refinement without retrieval, guideline-only generation, and straightforward patch-context extraction—leave unclear how much benefit requires the proposed architecture rather than additional inference or simpler preprocessing.

Baseline fidelity needs stronger justification. SecCoder's retriever is replaced, Codexity uses a substituted security tool, and several baselines suffer very large functionality losses without diagnostic analysis. Appendix D additionally treats locally deployed instruction-tuned models as completion models. These choices weaken the state-of-the-art comparison.

Claims of preserving functionality obscure meaningful regressions. On BigCodeBench, GPT-4o-mini drops from 54.6 to 45.2 and Llama3.1-8B from 36.0 to 31.8. On CodeGuard+, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B functionality drops from 88.3 to 80.6. Aggregate retention does not justify the conclusion of improvement 'without compromising functional correctness.'

The central slicing procedure is underspecified and inconsistent as written. Equation 3 and Algorithm 2 exclude zero-length paths and never explicitly add the patch statements themselves, potentially omitting the security fix. The algorithm also omits the described cross-version context reconciliation. Naming tree-sitter does not explain how sound data and control dependencies are constructed, and two-hop truncation cannot ensure contextual completeness.

Several interpretations exceed the evidence. Unseen CWE counts alone do not demonstrate improvements on unseen vulnerabilities; disaggregated results are needed. On Qwen, vulnerability-analysis-only retrieval achieves 66.2 SecurePass@1 versus 64.8 for all facets, and removing generation-time slicing achieves 66.1. Table 4 also includes a summarization configuration that underperforms unaugmented Llama, contradicting claims of consistent gains.

Reproducibility remains incomplete: the manuscript provides no implementation or constructed knowledge-base release, insufficient details on PDG construction and threshold selection, and an apparently incorrect 'Llama3.1-1B-Instruct' checkpoint name for CoSec. These gaps are material given the substantial baseline reimplementations.

Comparisons do not adequately isolate the proposed contribution. Missing controls include security-aware prompting without retrieval, compute-matched self-refinement, and stronger conventional retrieval using the same distilled knowledge. Generalization claims are unsupported by the reported analysis. Appendix B.4 counts benchmark CWE categories absent from the knowledge base but gives no performance breakdown on those categories. Their presence does not demonstrate improvement on unseen vulnerabilities. A benchmark-to-knowledge-base overlap audit is also missing.

Novelty is primarily an integration of established techniques: taxonomy-based grouping, recursive summarization, program slicing, multi-query retrieval, and rank fusion. The paper does not sufficiently position its contribution against hierarchical RAG and query expansion, or establish why its particular combination is necessary. For Qwen-7B, vulnerability-cause-only retrieval actually exceeds the full method, 66.2 versus 64.8 SecurePass@1.

The headline 4.8-point improvement is not clearly reconciled with Table 1. Appendix Table 5 suggests subtracting SafeCoder's 1.53-point average improvement from RESCUE's 6.28-point improvement, but those averages cover different model sets. A matched-model comparison and an explicit definition of the second-best baseline are needed.

Table 1 shows consistent SecurePass@1 improvements across all six models, including gains from 51.2 to 64.8 for Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and from 64.6 to 69.7 for DeepSeek-V3. Jointly measuring functionality and security avoids rewarding nonfunctional code that merely passes static checks.

The component ablations are substantial: they examine guideline extraction, slicing during retrieval versus generation, all seven facet combinations, hierarchy size, and alternative summarization models.
The appendix provides useful prompts, algorithms, dataset counts, and latency breakdowns. Slicing substantially reduces example length, and the framework does not require generator fine-tuning.
weaknesses: Security evidence comes from only 94 CodeGuard+ scenarios evaluated with CodeQL; the other three benchmarks measure functionality only. There are no independent security assessments, task-level confidence intervals, or paired significance tests. Generating 100 samples per task reduces sampling noise but does not establish robustness across security scenarios.

Section 3.3.2 explicitly selects k=4 based on CodeGuard+ performance, without describing a separate validation set. The selection procedure for retrieval thresholds is also unspecified. This creates a risk of evaluation-set tuning and weakens confidence in generalization.

The claim of preserving functionality is too strong. On BigCodeBench, GPT-4o-mini drops from 54.6 to 45.2, Llama3.1-8B from 36.0 to 31.8, and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B from 54.1 to 49.9. CodeGuard+ functionality also decreases for four of six models. Aggregate retention obscures practically meaningful regressions.

Baseline coverage is broad, but important controls are missing: security-aware prompting without retrieval, self-refinement using the same draft and vulnerability analysis, and a stronger flat retrieval baseline with comparable context and computation. Severe functionality collapses for several adapted baselines warrant implementation validation. Consequently, the contribution beyond additional inference and established retrieval techniques is not fully isolated.

The slicing specification has a concrete inconsistency: Equation 3 and Algorithm 2 require paths of length at least one and do not explicitly include the slicing seeds, so the security-relevant changed statements themselves need not be retained. The algorithm also omits the described cross-version context completion. PDG construction details beyond using tree-sitter are insufficient to resolve these issues.

Several conclusions exceed the evidence. CWE coverage counts alone do not demonstrate improvements on unseen vulnerability types; disaggregated results are needed. The complete facet combination is not uniformly best, with vulnerability-cause-only retrieval outperforming it on Qwen. Likewise, latency measurements on a 704-instance knowledge base do not establish scalability. These limitations, together with the evaluation concerns, leave the paper slightly below the acceptance threshold.

strengths: RESCUE addresses an important practical problem with a well-motivated combination of distilled security guidelines, patch-focused program slicing, and security-aware hierarchical retrieval.

Table 1 shows consistent SecurePass@1 improvements across all six models, averaging approximately 6.3 percentage points over zero-shot generation. Jointly evaluating functional correctness and security avoids rewarding nonfunctional but superficially secure outputs.

The additional CWEval experiments provide valuable dynamic-testing evidence beyond CodeQL: RESCUE outperforms both zero-shot generation and SecCoder across three models. Experiments on unseen vulnerability categories and programming languages further support transferability.

The evaluation includes substantial component ablations, alternative summarization models, retrieval-threshold analysis, and latency measurements. The slicing and guideline ablations provide concrete evidence that knowledge-base construction contributes to performance.
weaknesses: Evaluation independence is insufficiently established. Section 3.3.2 explicitly selects k=4 using CodeGuard+ performance, while Appendix C.6 uses 20 CodeGuard+ instances as validation data without stating that they are excluded from final evaluation. An independent development split and task-level confidence intervals are needed, particularly for small gains on only 94 scenarios. Generating 100 samples per task does not resolve uncertainty across tasks.

The claim of preserving functionality is overstated. On BigCodeBench, GPT-4o-mini falls from 54.6 to 45.2 and Llama3.1-8B from 36.0 to 31.8; CodeGuard+ functional Pass@1 drops from 88.3 to 80.6 for Qwen2.5-Coder-32B. Aggregate retention obscures meaningful model-specific regressions.

Comparisons do not sufficiently isolate the contribution over simpler alternatives. Missing controls include security prompting or self-refinement with comparable inference budgets, and retrieval of distilled guidelines without the full hierarchy. Closely related task-specific guideline retrieval work is cited but not evaluated. SecCoder's adapted retriever also makes the comparison less directly representative of the original method.

The slicing specification has a concrete correctness ambiguity: Algorithm 2 and Equation 3 require paths of length at least one and never explicitly include the patch statements themselves, so isolated points of interest can be omitted. The algorithm also does not specify the claimed cross-version context completion. Two-hop slicing cannot generally guarantee contextual completeness, and the implementation details for constructing semantic dependencies using tree-sitter are insufficient.

Several conclusions exceed the ablation evidence. For Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, vulnerability-cause retrieval alone scores 66.2 versus 64.8 for all three facets; removing slicing during generation also improves performance to 66.1. Threshold changes can reverse gains for Llama, and alternative summarizers sometimes underperform zero-shot. These results warrant a more qualified account of robustness and component necessity.

The novelty is primarily an integration of established summarization, slicing, hierarchical retrieval, and rank-fusion techniques. Stronger controlled comparisons and direct retrieval-quality measurements would better establish the distinctive contribution. Reproducibility is also incomplete: the supplied manuscript's code-availability statement has no link, and the CWEval sampling protocol and several static-analysis implementation details are unspecified.

strengths: RESCUE addresses an important practical problem with a coherent combination of distilled security guidelines, patch-focused program slicing, and hierarchical retrieval using complementary security cues.
